prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere products, predictable latency, documented quality). External: spacecraft, launch segment, user processing environments, conjunction data source. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time authority, pass supervision, anomaly response, contact schedule, routing policy, command engineering (command prep package from MPS); sends constraints to MPS; coordinates mode/priority with PPF; flight dynamics deliveries must state validity, frame, generation time, use. Command uplink needs MCC + Spacecraft Operations Team concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey) validates command stacks (syntax, timing, ranges, mode, baseline, burn plan); rejects unapproved/unprovenanced/expired/out-of-window items. Cybersecurity Desk reviews exceptions. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): orbit catalog; ephemerides/events to MCC, MPS, PPF; Star Tracker Mask File. Flight Dynamics Team: maneuver/collision screening; maneuver recommendation package to Spacecraft Operations Team; Ephemeris Delta Note. Orbit Determination Engine (S/X-Band station tracking): Doppler Residual Report, Laser Retroreflector Window. Mission Planning System (Cedar): authoritative timeline. Network Control System (Lantern): WAN, stations, links, timing; uses Security Exception Ticket to restrict transfer paths until containment; shall keep last validated routing config, reject unreviewed changes during product transfers. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): Primary Processing Cluster L0–L2; levels record build, calibration baseline, ancillary versions. Scheduler moves jobs to Backup Processing Cluster (same image/rules) if window missed; backup writes fallback provenance used by PQS. Both down: suspend, preserve raw in staging, notify MCC via event channel. Telemetry Ingest Service: immutable staging, Pass Replay Packet. Payload Calibration Team: approved calibration baseline, trend review; changes tested on sample scenes; specs updated if scale/alignment/saturation change. Product Quality Service: checks orbits; uses patch bundle; quality flags (missing packets, timing, saturation, cloud, geolocation, fallback) in metadata; produces Product Hold List. Delivery hold on failed checks/missing ancillary/blocking review; held products stay in staging. Long Term Archive (Granite): stores products tagged operational/test/reprocessed, orbit/maneuver/quality records; sends Storage Watermark Snapshot daily. Ground Network Manager.

Document units:
S176: Recovery after suspension prioritizes products with contractual latency commitments, then processes remaining scenes in acquisition order unless mission management approves a different backlog rule.
S177: Long Term Archive is the authoritative repository for Sentinel Vale raw downlink, auxiliary data, processing inputs, generated products, and operational metadata after routine production has completed.
S178: Archive admission begins only after Payload Processing Facility has delivered the product package, associated quality metadata, and checksum evidence required by the configured acceptance rule.
S179: Each accepted object is assigned a persistent identifier that remains stable across media migration, catalogue refresh, and later reprocessing campaigns.
S180: The repository stores object content separately from searchable metadata so that catalogue publication can proceed without exposing internal storage paths.
S181: Catalogue records are published to User Services Portal after Product Quality Service has set the public quality status and the embargo rule has been evaluated.
S182: Products under operational review remain discoverable only to authorized mission staff until the release condition is cleared.
S183: User Services Portal provides search, preview, order, and download functions through a browser interface and documented machine interfaces.
S184: Download services support resumable transfer, integrity verification, and rate controls that protect mission operations from excessive external demand.
S185: Registered users receive authorization scopes based on mission policy, contractual access rights, and applicable data licensing constraints.
S186: Anonymous access is allowed only for product classes that have been approved for open dissemination by mission management.
S187: Long Term Archive retains raw acquisition data for the life of the mission and for the post-mission preservation period defined in the archive policy.
S188: Standard Level 1 and Level 2 products are retained online while demand, contractual latency, or reprocessing dependence justifies low-latency access.
S189: Older product copies may be moved to lower-cost storage when catalogue metadata, checksums, and restore procedures remain available.
S190: Deletion is performed only against superseded temporary products, expired working copies, or objects covered by an approved disposal rule.
S191: Retention exceptions require traceability to the approving authority, the affected product classes, and the expected operational impact.
S192: Reprocessing is triggered when calibration improvements, processor corrections, orbit updates, or quality investigations materially change product fitness for use.
S193: Payload Calibration Team may request a reprocessing campaign when validation evidence shows a systematic radiometric or geometric issue.
S194: Mistral publishes orbit quality state changes to the archive operations queue before catalogue validity flags are updated.
